title: Secretary of State of Alabama

context.text: The seat is open: Secretary of State Wes Allen did not run for re-election; he announced a campaign for lieutenant governor. Dobson won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 65.5% over Christian Horn and Glenda Jackson; Rogers was unopposed for the Democratic nomination.

candidates.name: Caroleene Dobson

summary.text: Caroleene Dobson is the Republican nominee, a Montgomery attorney who was the 2024 Republican nominee in Alabama's 2nd Congressional District, losing to Rep. Shomari Figures with 45% of the vote. Her campaign centers on election-law enforcement and lower business fees.

background.text: Born and raised on her family's farm in Monroe County; holds an undergraduate degree from Harvard College and a law degree from Baylor University School of Law.
Shareholder at Maynard Nexsen in Montgomery, focusing on natural resources, commercial finance and real estate law.

priorities.text: Creating a dedicated team modeled on Florida's Election Crimes Division to investigate voter-fraud claims.
Reducing fees on Alabama businesses and providing same-day business services.

candidates.researchNotes: She has not held elected office. Her announcement-day statements did not address documentary proof of citizenship.

candidates.name: Wayne Rogers
candidates.currentRole: Executive Assistant to the Jefferson County Sheriff

summary.text: Wayne Rogers is the Democratic nominee, an attorney who has practiced in Alabama since 1988 and, since 2019, has worked as executive assistant to the Jefferson County sheriff. He lists ending straight-ticket voting, adopting early voting and letting absentee voters fix ballot defects as his key messages.

background.text: Native of Thomasville who has lived in Birmingham for 45 years; litigator who appeared in 66 of Alabama's 67 counties.
Serves on boards of mental-health entities and on the national board of Crisis Intervention Team International.

priorities.text: Adopting early voting; he notes Alabama is one of three states without it.
Allowing absentee voters to cure defective ballots.

candidates.researchNotes: He has not held elected office.

researchNotes: Slate confirmed against the Alabama Secretary of State's certified general-election candidate lists (Republican and Democratic Party certifications, dated August 26, 2026; the independent-candidate certification lists no statewide candidates). No independent or third-party candidate for this office was found. A Libertarian candidate appeared in 2022; none was found for 2026.
